topic: 3D HSR — roughing counterpart to 3D HSM finishing; rapid bulk material removal with smooth high-speed motion
tip: InventorCAM 2024 3D HSR is the roughing module paired with 3D HSM finishing — same gouge-free, smooth-toolpath, retract-optimized core but emphasizing maximum MRR via large stepdowns + high feeds rather than fine surface generation. Always sequence HSR (bulk) → HSM (semi-finish) → finishing strategy (SWARF / morphed / pencil). Stock from HSR is the input to HSM; the two share the same Stock Model so HSM only cuts what HSR left.

topic: HSR strategy taxonomy — Roughing / Rest Roughing / Plunge Roughing / Adaptive Roughing
tip: 3D HSR ships 4 first-class strategies: (1) Roughing — pocket-style stepdowns over the whole stock; (2) Rest Roughing — uses Stock Model to cut only the material a prior op left (10-40% cycle-time savings vs blind re-rough); (3) Plunge Roughing — Z-axis-only entries for high-aspect-ratio cavities where helix entry is geometrically impossible; (4) Adaptive Roughing (the iMachining-equivalent) — constant chip load via dynamic stepover; the only strategy that supports full flute engagement on hardened material without thermal failure. Pick by stock geometry, not by habit.

topic: Stock Model is the load-bearing input — rest-roughing without it falls back to blind re-rough
tip: 3D HSR's Rest Roughing strategy REQUIRES a Stock Model — a CAD body representing remaining material after the previous op. Without it, the strategy degrades silently to a full re-rough (huge air-cutting penalty). Stock Models are generated automatically when prior ops are run with 'Update Stock' enabled in the Operation tree; manually-imported STL is also valid. Always verify the Stock Model exists + is current (re-generate after editing prior ops) BEFORE running Rest Roughing on a high-cycle-cost setup.

topic: Trochoidal + dynamic entries — full-slot cutting without breaking the tool
tip: In 3D HSR, Trochoidal entry replaces ramp/helix for slot widths < 1.5× tool dia (where helix can't fit). Tool follows tight circles inside the slot rim — radial engagement stays low (~20% of tool dia) while axial engagement runs full flute. Dynamic entries (Adaptive Roughing's default) modulate stepover continuously to hold a target chip load. Both prevent the catastrophic tool failure that blind plunge or full-slot conventional cutting cause on titanium/Inconel. Never disable adaptive/trochoidal on slot-dominated parts to 'save planning time' — the recovery is hours of tool/spindle/part scrap.

topic: High-feed milling (HFM) — light DOC, very high feed; alternative to deep-DOC heavy roughing
tip: 3D HSR supports the High-Feed Milling regime — axial DOC 0.5-1.5 mm but feed-per-tooth 1.5-3.0 mm (vs 0.05-0.15 in normal roughing) yielding ~20× higher feed rate. The mechanic: chip thinning at low axial engagement means actual chip load matches normal milling while the table moves 20× faster. Requires (a) a face/insert tool rated for HFM (button or octagonal inserts, large lead angle), (b) rigid spindle taper (HSK/CAPTO preferred over BT), (c) toolpath smoothness ≥ G2/G3 arcs (no G1-G1 corners — feed-rate dump kills the gain). Best on flat-stock-removal pre-rough; less suited to deep cavities.

topic: Chip thinning compensation — feed correction at varying radial engagement
tip: When radial engagement drops below 50% of tool diameter (typical in HSR adaptive/HFM modes), actual chip thickness is LESS than commanded feed-per-tooth — by a factor of sqrt(1 - (1-2·ae/D)²). Without compensation, the tool runs under-loaded → rubbing, work-hardening, premature flank wear. 3D HSR's Chip Thinning Compensation toggle adjusts F = F_nominal · (D/(2·ae))^0.5 (approximate) so actual chip load hits the spec. Always enable for ae/D < 0.3; disable only for full-slot or > 50% radial engagement where the math inverts (over-loading).

topic: Toolpath smoothing — fillet sharp corners + arc-fit linears for sustained high feeds
tip: 3D HSR's Smoothing parameter replaces sharp G1-G1 direction changes with G2/G3 arcs of a specified radius (typically 5-15% of tool dia). Without smoothing, controllers must decelerate to zero at every corner (look-ahead buffer can't process infinite jerk) — measured feed-rate dump 30-70% on high-feed paths. Smoothing radius too large → leaves uncut corners (rest material for the next op); too small → marginal improvement. Default 10% tool dia is a safe starting point; raise on hardened material (more time saved than corner accuracy lost since rest-roughing recovers it).

topic: HSR → HSM transition checklist — Stock Model + Stock-to-Leave + Z-band overlap
tip: Safe HSR→HSM handoff requires 3 things: (1) HSR ends with a Stock Model export (Operation tree 'Update Stock' enabled); (2) HSR Stock-to-Leave is set ≥ HSM tool's planned step-down (default 0.3-0.5 mm — HSM can't cut what's not there, and over-leaving stock starves HSM of work); (3) HSM Z-band overlap ≥ HSR's largest stepdown (otherwise HSM's first plunge into untouched-by-HSR shallow areas hits full stock height — collision risk). Check all three before running the HSM op; the Operation tree's Stock Visualization (F7 in InventorCAM) shows exactly what HSM will see.
